_note: General stage playbook, used when the AI expert is unavailable. Same content as the frontend's general mock.

stages.summary: The crop is getting established. An even stand now sets up the rest of the season.

steps.title: Keep the seedbed moist
steps.why: Seeds and young plants need steady moisture to establish evenly.

steps.title: Check the stand for gaps
steps.why: Gaps found early can still be replanted.

watchFor: Seedlings dying off in wet, cold soil

stages.summary: The plants are building leaves and roots. Keep competition and pests down.

steps.title: Control weeds early
steps.why: Weeds take the most yield while the crop is young.

steps.title: Feed the crop if it looks pale
steps.why: Pale, slow growth often means the crop needs nutrients.

steps.title: Scout for pests weekly
steps.why: Pests are cheapest to manage before numbers build up.

stages.summary: The crop is flowering or forming its harvest. Stress now costs the most.

steps.title: Keep water steady
steps.why: Drought during flowering and fruit set does the most damage.

steps.title: Check leaves for disease
steps.why: Disease spreads fast in warm, humid weather.

stages.summary: The harvest is filling out. Protect it and get ready to harvest.

steps.title: Plan the harvest
steps.why: Harvesting at the right moment protects both yield and quality.

stages.summary: The season is done. Harvest promptly and write down what you learned.

steps.title: Harvest
steps.why: Delays risk weather damage and lower quality.

steps.title: Record the yield
steps.why: Your own numbers make next season's plan sharper than any average.
